description: Extract useSessionTimeline's directly-extractable event reducers into a React-independent model/session-timeline-reducer.ts, converge the hook into an event-wiring thin layer, and remove the dead taskProgress/loopProgress state — test-first, behavior-preserving.

tasks.title: Remove dead state taskProgress/loopProgress
tasks.description: Delete the never-set `taskProgress` (`TaskProgressMap`) and `loopProgress` (`LoopProgress`) `useState` declarations and return fields from useSessionTimeline.ts, and drop the corresponding props, `TaskProgressPanel` render branch (`currentStage === 'build' && taskEntries.length > 0`), `taskEntries` derivation, and `TaskProgressMap`/`LoopProgress` imports from SessionTimeline.tsx. Update SessionTimeline.test.tsx render fixtures to drop the two removed props. The rendered DOM is observably identical because the panel never rendered with a non-empty task list. Keep `TaskProgressPanel`/`TaskStatusIcon` as exports (deletion is out of scope).
acceptanceCriteria: useSessionTimeline.ts contains no `useState<TaskProgressMap>` or `useState<LoopProgress>` and its returned object has no `taskProgress` or `loopProgress` keys
useSessionTimeline.ts drops `TaskProgressMap`/`LoopProgress` from the `entities/coder-session` import

SessionTimeline.tsx props interface no longer mentions `taskProgress`/`loopProgress`, no longer imports `TaskProgressMap`/`LoopProgress`, and no longer renders the `TaskProgressPanel` element under any condition
SessionTimeline.test.tsx render fixtures no longer pass `taskProgress`/`loopProgress` props
`TaskProgressPanel` and `TaskStatusIcon` remain exported from SessionTimeline.tsx (no contract change)
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` is green
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` is green with no rendered-output regression
tasks.output: Slimmed useSessionTimeline.ts return shape (drops taskProgress/loopProgress) and SessionTimeline.tsx without the dead build-stage panel branch
tasks.notes: Zero behavioral risk — the Map was never written so the panel gate was always false (design D6). Goes first to slim the return shape the rest of the work targets (design D8 step 1).

tasks.title: Add event-wiring integration tests before reducer extraction
tasks.description: Add `dispatchAgentEvent(...)`-driven integration tests to useSessionTimeline.test.ts covering the previously-uncovered event wiring for `plan_round_start`, `plan_round_complete`, `coder_recovery_status`, `session.liveness`, `compaction_event`, `com.mohist.agent-session.context-compacted`, `com.mohist.agent-session.context-health-updated`, and `tool_call.started`/`updated`/`completed`, plus a `plan_session_update` batch + 100ms cadence assertion. Use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.setSystemTime()` per testing.md §2 (no wall clock). These tests pin current hook behavior and are the regression net that makes the subsequent reducer extraction safe; they must land and pass against the current (pre-extraction) hook code.
acceptanceCriteria: useSessionTimeline.test.ts gains `dispatchAgentEvent`-driven cases for every listed event, each asserting the resulting hook state (rounds / recoveryStatus / planProgress / contextHealth as applicable)

A `plan_session_update` cadence test uses fake timers to assert that two events within a 100ms window coalesce into a single `setRounds` flush and that the rAF/setTimeout branch matches the elapsed-since-last-flush rule
A `tool_call.started` → `updated` → `completed` test asserts the shared `liveToolCallMapRef` in-place mutation semantics and the `timeout` → `failed` state mapping
All new tests pass against the current hook code (the slimmed shape from T-001) before any reducer extraction
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` is green
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` is green
tasks.output: Extended useSessionTimeline.test.ts with event-wiring + batch/cadence integration coverage (green against pre-extraction hook)
tasks.notes: Spec mandates test-first: these tests MUST exist and pass before T-003 begins (design D8 step 2). They cover wiring that had zero direct coverage, so they are a standalone coverage deliverable, not the tests for the extracted reducers (those are co-located in T-003).

tasks.title: Extract pure event reducers to model/session-timeline-reducer.ts
tasks.description: Create `model/session-timeline-reducer.ts` holding the nine directly-extractable event reducers (`plan_round_start`, `plan_round_complete`, `coder_recovery_status`, `session.liveness`, `usage.updated`, `context_health_update`, `compaction_event`, `com.mohist.agent-session.context-compacted`, `com.mohist.agent-session.context-health-updated`) as pure `(prev, detail, env) => next` functions where `env` carries `{ now, isoNow, randomId }` (design D2), plus the shared types/helpers they own (`Round`, `RecoveryEvent`, `RecoveryStatus`, `PlanStep`, `PlanProgress`, `ContextHealthState`, `ContextHealthStatus`, `CompactionEntry`, `toContextHealthStatus`, `mapLivenessToRecoveryStatus`, `BASE_PLAN_STEPS`), `deriveToolCallTitle`, `reconstructRoundsFromEvents`, and a pure `mergeContextHealth` dedup helper (design D4). Each reducer takes and returns the full state slice object `{ rounds, planProgress, recoveryStatus, contextHealth }` (design D3). Rewrite each of the nine subscription closures in useSessionTimeline.ts to delegate to the matching reducer via `setX(updater)`. Re-export the shared symbols from useSessionTimeline.ts so SessionTimeline.tsx and PlanProgressPanel.tsx import paths resolve unchanged (design D7). Keep `plan_session_update`/`flushPlanBuffer`/`scheduleFlush`/`handleToolEvent` and the `liveToolCallMapRef` sharing in the hook unchanged (design D5). Add co-located `model/session-timeline-reducer.test.ts` exercising each reducer as a pure function with a fixed `env`.
acceptanceCriteria: `model/session-timeline-reducer.ts` exists and exports the nine reducers, the shared types/helpers, `deriveToolCallTitle`, `reconstructRoundsFromEvents`, and `mergeContextHealth`

The reducer module imports nothing from `react` or `@tanstack/react-query`, references no `requestAnimationFrame`/`window.setTimeout`/`Date.now()`, and declares no module-level mutable `let`/`var` bindings
Each of the nine reducers is a pure `(prev, detail, env) => next` function returning a new value without mutating `prev`

useSessionTimeline.ts's nine subscription closures delegate state transitions to the extracted reducers; the hook body retains only the session-scoping predicate, the `env` construction, and the `setX(updater)` wiring

`plan_session_update` → `flushPlanBuffer` → `scheduleFlush` and `handleToolEvent` stay in the hook with the 100ms rAF/setTimeout cadence and `liveToolCallMapRef` set/get/in-place-mutation semantics unchanged

useSessionTimeline.ts re-exports the shared symbols so `SessionTimeline.tsx` (`../model/useSessionTimeline`) and `PlanProgressPanel.tsx` (`../../coder-session/model/useSessionTimeline`) imports resolve unchanged
`model/session-timeline-reducer.test.ts` exercises each exported reducer as a pure function with a fixed `env` (including `mergeContextHealth` dedup and the self-review FAIL step extension)
T-002 integration tests and the pre-existing behavioral cases (`usage.updated`/`context_health_update`/`compaction_event` pinned by issue-247) remain green unchanged
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` is green
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` is green
tasks.output: model/session-timeline-reducer.ts (nine pure reducers + shared types/helpers + dedup) + slimmed useSessionTimeline.ts (event-wiring thin layer) + model/session-timeline-reducer.test.ts
tasks.notes: Follows design D1–D7. env-injection (D2) keeps reducers deterministic and unit-testable; state-object in/out (D3) keeps multi-slice transitions atomic; re-export (D7) avoids any public/import-path change. Reducer unit tests are co-located here per the no-separate-test-task rule.
